newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pulls back from highs as specs sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pulls back from highs as specs sell.

text.p: Robusta futures retreated slightly from their fresh surge on Wednesday as some speculators who bought early ahead of New York sold back in the afternoon.
But prices still finished the day higher, with benchmark May holding above the $1,610 level.
Fund and trade buying took the front-month May to its intraday peak of $1,650, the highest in two weeks, after news of a smaller-than-expected rise in the U.S. March green coffee stocks.
The news came after the New York market had closed on Tuesday.
"The specs were buying this morning on the news as a precaution before New York opening. And when New York opens they liquidate in London," said one.
London's May closed $37 up at $1,615 while most-active July was $35 firmer at $1,630 but below its intraday high of $1,668.
The fund buying emerged after the market triggered buy-stops at $1,600 and then $1,620 on July.
New York's May arabica futures were driven to a high of 213 cents a lb in early trade on the stock news before trading at 210 cents by 1633 GMT.
The Green Coffee Association of New York reported coffee stocks in U.S. warehouses rose by a modest 111,000 60-kg bags to 1.65 million in March.
This was below earlier market expectations of a 200,000 to 300,000 bag increase. There was even talk earlier on Tuesday of a build of up to 700,000.
"This should therefore be seen as positive, but there will undoubtedly be some talk that the difference will show up next month," broker GNI said earlier on Wednesday.
Despite the rise, robustas continued to trail arabica prices, with the May/May arbitrage holding at a wide 134 cents.
In LIFFE options, the May position went off the board on Wednesday without any fireworks. Attention centred on July which saw keen interest in calls options.
Volume reached 696 lots with July $1,750 and $1,900 calls topping the active list.
